title: Track performance as delayed labels arrive
problem: Labels for a prediction arrive days later, and some never arrive. A monitor that reports the last known accuracy looks healthy exactly when it knows nothing, and one that computes accuracy over the few labels that have arrived reports a number biased toward whatever gets labeled first.
context: Builds on drift statistics. Labels arrive as their own synthetic stream keyed to predictions, with a declared expected delay.
impact: This is what turns drift from a hint into evidence of degradation, and what stops the monitor from reporting health it cannot know.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Labels are joined to predictions by identity as they arrive. A label for an unknown prediction is reported, not silently dropped.
Performance for a period is computed only over labeled predictions and is always reported with its label coverage.
A period with no labels, or coverage below a declared minimum, reports performance as unknown, never as the last known value or as healthy.
When late labels arrive, the affected period's performance is recomputed and the change recorded, without rewriting the earlier result.

Automated tests cover a fully labeled period, a period with no labels, a low-coverage period, a late label that changes a result, and a label for an unknown prediction, and pass at the submitted revision.
The learner explains the coverage rule, one rejected alternative (for example imputing missing labels), and how label arrival order could bias the reported performance.

constraints: Standard library plus a test runner only.
No network access and no model API. Every input is synthetic and generated or checked in by the learner.
Do not implement alerting or the runbook yet.
Do not push to a remote or open a pull request as part of this task.

scope.description: A join of delayed labels to predictions and an honest performance metric over it.

investigation_areas: What a performance number means when only some labels have arrived
Which labels tend to arrive first in practice, and how that biases early numbers
How a recomputed period is recorded without losing what was reported before
testing_expectations: Run the project's own test suite. State the exact command in the design; the learner chooses the runner and the layout.
documentation_requirements: Record the join, the coverage rule, the recomputation policy and the rejected alternative in the learner design.
